title.zh: 卷一百三十九 志1: 天文志
title.raw: 卷一百三十九 志1: 天文志 Volume 139: Treatises 1 Astronomy

sentences.zh: 天文志

translations.literal: Treatise on Astronomy
translations.idiomatic: Astronomical Treatise

sentences.zh: 〈（案：《薛史天文志序》《永樂大典》原闕，然其日食、星變諸門，事跡具存，較《歐陽史·司天考》為詳備。

translations.literal: (Note: The preface to the Astronomical Treatise in the Xue History and the Yongle Encyclopedia are originally missing; yet the sections on solar eclipses, stellar anomalies, and the like have their events fully preserved, and are more detailed and complete than the "Treatise on the Heavenly Offices" in Ouyang Xiu's History.)
translations.idiomatic: (Editor's note: The preface to the Astronomical Treatise in Xue Juzheng's History and the Yongle Encyclopedia are lost in the sources we have, but the chapters on solar eclipses, stellar changes, and related topics survive with their records intact and are fuller than the Heavenly Offices treatise in Ouyang Xiu's New History.)

sentences.zh: 今考《五代會要》所載星變、物異諸門，與《司天考》互有詳略。

translations.literal: Examining now the sections on stellar changes and prodigies recorded in the Essentials of Government in the Five Dynasties, each has details and omissions when compared with the Treatise on the Heavenly Offices.
translations.idiomatic: A comparison of the stellar-change and prodigy sections in the Essentials of Government in the Five Dynasties with the Heavenly Offices treatise shows that each account is more detailed in some places and thinner in others.

sentences.zh: 蓋五代典章散佚，各記所聞，未能畫一也。

translations.literal: This is because the institutions and records of the Five Dynasties were scattered and lost; each work recorded what it heard, and could not be made uniform.
translations.idiomatic: The institutions and archives of the Five Dynasties had largely dispersed; each compiler wrote down what came to hand, so the records could not be harmonized into a single standard.

sentences.zh: 參考諸書，當以《薛史》為得其實焉。）〉

translations.literal: Consulting the various books, the Xue History should be taken as obtaining the facts.)〉
translations.idiomatic: On balance, the Xue History should be regarded as closest to what actually happened.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁太祖乾化元年，正月丙戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianhua of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on the first day of the first month (bingxu), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianhua under Liang Taizu, on the new moon of the first month (bingxu), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 時言事諸臣，多引漢高祖末年日蝕於歲首，太祖甚惡之，於是素服避正殿，百官各守本司。

translations.literal: At the time the remonstrating officials mostly cited the solar eclipse at the year's beginning in the final years of Emperor Gaozu of Han; Taizu greatly detested this, and therefore wore plain garments and avoided the main hall; the hundred officials each remained at their offices.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrating ministers of the day mostly invoked the solar eclipse at the year's opening in the closing years of Han Gaozu; Taizu took this as a very bad omen, put on undyed robes, withdrew from the main audience hall, and ordered every official to remain at his post.

sentences.zh: 是日，有司奏：「雲初陰晦，事同不蝕。」

translations.literal: On that day the responsible offices reported: "At first the clouds were dark and overcast; the matter is the same as if there were no eclipse."
translations.idiomatic: That day the responsible offices reported: "Clouds were dark from the outset, so in effect no eclipse was seen."

sentences.zh: 百僚奉表稱賀。

translations.literal: The hundred officials submitted memorials offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The entire bureaucracy submitted memorials of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 末帝寵德三年，十月辛未朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde of the Last Emperor, on the first day of the tenth month (xinwei), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongde under the Last Emperor, on the new moon of the tenth month (xinwei), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗同光三年，四月癸亥朔，時有司奏：「日蝕在卯，主歲大旱。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, on the first day of the fourth month (guihai), at the time the responsible offices reported: "The solar eclipse is in mao; it presages a great drought for the year."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang under Tang Zhuangzong, on the new moon of the fourth month (guihai), the astronomical office reported: "The eclipse falls in the mao hour and portends a severe drought for the year."

sentences.zh: 明宗天成元年，八月乙酉朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng of Emperor Mingzong, on the first day of the eighth month (yiyou), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng under Mingzong, on the new moon of the eighth month (yiyou), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 二年，八月己卯朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the first day of the eighth month (jimao), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the new moon of the eighth month (jimao), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 三年，二月丁丑朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the first day of the second month (dingchou), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on the new moon of the second month (dingchou), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 其日陰雲不見，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: On that day clouds were overcast and it was not seen; the hundred officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds obscured the sky that day so the eclipse was not visible, and the officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，六月癸巳朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing, on the first day of the sixth month (guisi), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changxing, on the new moon of the sixth month (guisi), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 其日陰冥不見，至夕大雨。

translations.literal: On that day it was dark and overcast and not seen; by evening there was heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: The sky was dark and the eclipse could not be seen; heavy rain fell by evening.

sentences.zh: 二年，十一月甲申朔，先是，司天奏：「朔日合食二分，伏緣所蝕微少，太陽光影相鑠，伏恐不辨虧闕，請其日不入閣。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the first day of the eleventh month (jiashen), beforehand the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "On the new-moon day there should be an eclipse of two parts in ten; we submit that because the portion eclipsed is very slight, the sun's light and shadow will blend together, and we fear the deficiency will not be distinguishable; we request that on that day Your Majesty not enter the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the new moon of the eleventh month (jiashen), the astronomical office had earlier reported: "A two-tenths eclipse is due on the new moon; because the obscuration will be slight, sun and shadow may merge so that the bite in the disk cannot be made out—we ask that Your Majesty not enter the inner court that day.

sentences.zh: 百官守司。」

translations.literal: The hundred officials are to remain at their offices."
translations.idiomatic: Officials are to remain at their posts."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The request] was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖天福二年，正月乙卯，先是，司天奏：「正月二日，太陽虧蝕，宜避正殿，開諸營門，蓋藏兵器，半月不宜用軍。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu of Jin, on yimao of the first month, beforehand the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "On the second day of the first month the sun will suffer eclipse; it is appropriate to avoid the main hall, open the gates of the various camps, cover and store weapons, and for half a month it is not appropriate to use the army."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu under Jin Gaozu, on yimao of the first month, the astronomical office had reported in advance: "On the second day of the first month the sun will be eclipsed; the emperor should withdraw from the main hall, the camp gates should be opened, arms should be stored away, and troops should not be employed for half a month."

sentences.zh: 是日太陽虧，十分內食三分，在尾宿十七度。

translations.literal: On that day the sun was eclipsed; within ten parts, three parts were eaten, at the seventeenth degree of the Tail mansion.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sun was eclipsed: three parts in ten were covered, at the seventeenth degree of the Tail asterism.

sentences.zh: 日出東方，以帶蝕三分，漸生，至卯時復滿。

translations.literal: The sun rose in the east with a belt-like eclipse of three parts; it gradually regenerated, and by the mao hour was full again.
translations.idiomatic: The sun rose in the east with a three-part belt eclipse, then waxed back until by the mao hour it was whole again.

sentences.zh: 三年，正月戊申朔，司天先奏，其日日蝕。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the first day of the first month (wushen), the Directorate of Astronomy had reported in advance that on that day the sun would be eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on the new moon of the first month (wushen), the astronomical office had foretold an eclipse for that day.

sentences.zh: 至是日不蝕，內外稱賀。

translations.literal: When that day came there was no eclipse; inside and outside the court offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived there was no eclipse, and court and capital alike offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 四年，七月庚子朔，時中書門下奏：「謹按舊禮：日有變，天子素服避正殿，太史以所司救日於社，陳五兵、五鼓、五麾，東戟西矛，南弩北楯，中央置鼓，服從其位，百職廢務，素服守司，重列於庭，每等異位，向日而立，明復而止。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the first day of the seventh month (gengzi), at the time the Secretariat and Chancellery reported: "We respectfully examine the old rites: when the sun undergoes change, the Son of Heaven wears plain garments and avoids the main hall; the Grand Astrologer, according to his office, performs the rite to rescue the sun at the altar of the soil, displaying the five weapons, five drums, and five banners—halberds to the east, spears to the west, crossbows to the south, shields to the north, with a drum placed in the center—garments according to position; the hundred offices suspend duties, wear plain garments and remain at their offices, arrayed in ranks in the court, each grade in a different position, standing facing the sun until brightness is restored, then stopping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the new moon of the seventh month (gengzi), the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "According to the ancient rites, when the sun shows an anomaly the emperor puts on undyed robes and leaves the main hall; the chief astrologer performs the sun-rescue rite at the soil altar, arraying five kinds of arms, five drums, and five banners—halberds east, spears west, crossbows south, shields north, with a drum in the center—each in prescribed dress; all offices suspend business, wear plain clothes and keep their posts, and line up in the courtyard by rank, each grade in its place, facing the sun until full daylight returns.

sentences.zh: 今所司法物，鹹不能具，去歲正旦日食，唯謹藏兵仗，皇帝避正殿素食，百官守司。

translations.literal: The ritual objects in the charge of the offices today cannot all be provided; at last year's New Year's Day solar eclipse, we only carefully stored away weapons, the emperor avoided the main hall and ate plain food, and the hundred officials remained at their offices.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual implements now in the keeping of the offices cannot all be supplied; at last year's New Year eclipse we could only store arms with care, have the emperor withdraw to plain fare in a side hall, and keep officials at their posts.

sentences.zh: 今且欲依近禮施行。」

translations.literal: For now we wish to carry out the recent rites."
translations.idiomatic: We propose to follow the simplified rites used in recent years."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The memorial] was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 七年，四月甲寅朔，是日百官守司，太陽不蝕，上表稱賀。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on the first day of the fourth month (jiayin), on that day the hundred officials remained at their offices; the sun was not eclipsed, and memorials of congratulation were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, on the new moon of the fourth month (jiayin), officials kept their posts as ordered; the sun was not eclipsed, and congratulatory memorials were sent up.

sentences.zh: 八年，四月戊申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, on the first day of the fourth month (wushen), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, on the new moon of the fourth month (wushen), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 少帝開運元年，九月庚午朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun of the Young Emperor, on the first day of the ninth month (gengwu), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiyun under the Young Emperor, on the new moon of the ninth month (gengwu), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 二年，八月甲子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the first day of the eighth month (jiazi), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the new moon of the eighth month (jiazi), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 三年，二月壬戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the first day of the second month (renxu), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on the new moon of the second month (renxu), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 漢隱帝乾祐三年，十一月甲子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianyou of Emperor Yindi of Han, on the first day of the eleventh month (jiazi), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianyou under Han Yindi, on the new moon of the eleventh month (jiazi), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 周太祖廣順二年，四月丙戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Emperor Taizu of Zhou, on the first day of the fourth month (bingxu), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangshun under Zhou Taizu, on the new moon of the fourth month (bingxu), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 月食

translations.literal: Lunar Eclipses
translations.idiomatic: Lunar Eclipses

sentences.zh: 梁太祖開平四年，十二月十四日夜，先是，司天奏：「是日月蝕，不宜用兵。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiping of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on the night of the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, beforehand the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "On this day there will be a lunar eclipse; it is not appropriate to use the army."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiping under Liang Taizu, on the night of the fourteenth of the twelfth month, the astronomical office had reported in advance: "A lunar eclipse is due; troops should not be deployed."

sentences.zh: 時王景仁方總大軍北伐，追之不及。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jingren was just then commanding the great army on a northern campaign; [the order] could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingren was already leading the main army north; the warning could not reach him in time.

sentences.zh: 至五年正月二日，果為後唐莊宗大敗於柏鄉。

translations.literal: By the second day of the first month of the fifth year, he was indeed greatly defeated by Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang at Boxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the first month of the fifth year he was indeed routed by Later Tang Zhuangzong at Boxiang.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗同光三年，三月戊申，月蝕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, on wushen of the third month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang under Tang Zhuangzong, on wushen of the third month, there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 九月甲辰，月蝕。

translations.literal: On jiachen of the ninth month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen of the ninth month there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 明宗天成三年，十二月乙卯，月蝕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng of Emperor Mingzong, on yimao of the twelfth month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancheng under Mingzong, on yimao of the twelfth month, there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 四年，六月癸丑望，月食。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the full moon of guichou of the sixth month, there was a lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the full moon (guichou) of the sixth month, the moon was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚戌，月蝕。

translations.literal: On gengxu of the twelfth month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu of the twelfth month there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖天福二年，七月丙寅，月蝕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu of Jin, on bingyin of the seventh month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu under Jin Gaozu, on bingyin of the seventh month there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 五年，十一月丁丑，月蝕鶉首之分。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on dingchou of the eleventh month, the moon was eclipsed within the Hare's Head asterism division.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on dingchou of the eleventh month the moon was eclipsed within the Hare's Head celestial division.

sentences.zh: 少帝開運元年，三月戊子，月蝕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun of the Young Emperor, on wuzi of the third month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiyun under the Young Emperor, on wuzi of the third month there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 九月丙戌，月蝕。

translations.literal: On bingxu of the ninth month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu of the ninth month there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖天福十二年，十二月乙未，月食。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu of Han, on yiwei of the twelfth month, there was a lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianfu under Han Gaozu, on yiwei of the twelfth month the moon was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 周世宗顯德三年，正月戊申，月蝕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande of Emperor Shizong of Zhou, on wushen of the first month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande under Zhou Shizong, on wushen of the first month, there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 五年，十一月辛未，月蝕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on xinwei of the eleventh month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on xinwei of the eleventh month, there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: ◎月暈

translations.literal: ◎ Lunar Halos
translations.idiomatic: Lunar Halos

sentences.zh: 唐明宗天成元年，十一月，月暈匝火、木。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, in the eleventh month, the moon had a halo encircling the Fire and Wood [planetary stations].
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng under Tang Mingzong, in the eleventh month the moon showed a halo ringed around the stations of Fire and Wood.

sentences.zh: ◎彗孛梁太祖乾化二年，四月甲戌夜，彗見於靈臺之西。

translations.literal: ◎ Comets and Broom Stars. In the second year of Qianhua of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on the night of jiaxu of the fourth month, a comet appeared west of the Observatory Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Comets and Broom Stars. In the second year of Qianhua under Liang Taizu, on the night of jiaxu in the fourth month, a comet appeared west of the Observatory Terrace.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗天成三年，十月庚午夜，西南有孛，長丈餘，東南指，在牛宿五度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, on the night of gengwu of the tenth month, in the southwest there was a broom star more than a zhang in length, pointing southeast, at the fifth degree of the Ox mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancheng under Tang Mingzong, on the night of gengwu in the tenth month, a broom star more than ten feet long appeared in the southwest, its tail toward the southeast, at the fifth degree of the Ox asterism.

sentences.zh: 末帝清泰三年，九月己丑，彗出虛、危，長尺餘，形細微，經天壘、哭星。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingtai of the Last Emperor, on jichou of the ninth month, a comet issued from Emptiness and Rooftop, more than a chi in length, its form slight and fine, passing through the Celestial Ramparts and the Weeping Star.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qingtai under the Last Emperor, on jichou of the ninth month a comet rose from the Emptiness and Rooftop asterisms, a little over a foot long and faint in form, crossing the Celestial Ramparts and the Weeping Star.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖天福六年，九月，有彗星長丈餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu of Jin, in the ninth month, there was a comet more than a zhang in length.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu under Jin Gaozu, in the ninth month a comet appeared more than ten feet long.

sentences.zh: 八年，十月庚戌夜，有彗見於東方，西指，尾長一丈，在角九度。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, on the night of gengxu of the tenth month, a comet was seen in the east, pointing west; its tail was one zhang in length, at the ninth degree of the Horn mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, on the night of gengxu in the tenth month, a comet appeared in the east with its tail toward the west, ten feet long, at the ninth degree of the Horn asterism.

sentences.zh: 周太祖顯德三年，正月壬戌夜，有星孛於參角，其芒指於東南。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande of Emperor Taizu of Zhou, on the night of renxu of the first month, there was a broom star at the corner of the Three Stars mansion; its rays pointed toward the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande under Zhou Taizu, on the night of renxu in the first month a broom star appeared at the corner of the Three Stars asterism, its rays toward the southeast.

sentences.zh: ◎五星淩犯梁太祖開平二年，正月乙亥，歲星犯月。

translations.literal: ◎ Encroachments of the Five Planets. In the second year of Kaiping of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on yihai of the first month, the Year Star encroached upon the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Encroachments of the Five Planets. In the second year of Kaiping under Liang Taizu, on yihai of the first month Jupiter crossed the moon's path.

sentences.zh: 乾化二年，五月壬戌，熒惑犯心大星，去心四度，順行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianhua, on renxu of the fifth month, Mars encroached upon the great star of the Heart mansion, four degrees from the Heart, moving in direct motion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianhua, on renxu of the fifth month Mars encroached on the chief star of the Heart asterism, four degrees from the Heart, in direct motion.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「心為帝王之星。」

translations.literal: The prognostication says: "The Heart is the star of the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The omen text reads: "The Heart is the star of the sovereign."

sentences.zh: 其年六月五日，帝崩。

translations.literal: In that year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗同光二年，八月戊子，熒惑犯星。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, on wuzi of the eighth month, Mars encroached upon the Star mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongguang under Tang Zhuangzong, on wuzi of the eighth month Mars encroached on the Star asterism.

sentences.zh: 三年，三月丙申，熒惑犯上相。

translations.literal: In the third year, on bingshen of the third month, Mars encroached upon the Upper Minister star.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on bingshen of the third month Mars encroached on the Upper Minister star.

sentences.zh: 四月甲申，熒惑犯左執法。

translations.literal: On jiashen of the fourth month, Mars encroached upon the Left Enforcer star.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen of the fourth month Mars encroached on the Left Enforcer star.

sentences.zh: 六月丙寅，歲犯右執法。

translations.literal: On bingyin of the sixth month, the Year Star encroached upon the Right Enforcer star.

translations.idiomatic: On jisi of the intercalary fifth month Jupiter was visible in daylight.

sentences.zh: 八月戊子，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On wuzi of the eighth month, Venus was seen by day.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi of the eighth month Venus was visible in daylight.

sentences.zh: 三年，十月壬申，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the third year, on renshen of the tenth month, Venus was seen by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on renshen of the tenth month Venus was visible in daylight.

sentences.zh: 四年，五月癸卯，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on guimao of the fifth month, Venus was seen by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on guimao of the fifth month Venus was visible in daylight.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年，五月己未，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingtai, on jiwei of the fifth month, Venus was seen by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingtai, on jiwei of the fifth month Venus was visible in daylight.

sentences.zh: 漢天福十三年，四月丙子，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianfu of Han, on bingzi of the fourth month, Venus was seen by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianfu under Han, on bingzi of the fourth month Venus was visible in daylight.

sentences.zh: 乾祐二年，四月壬午，太白晝見，

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyou, on renwu of the fourth month, Venus was seen by day,
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyou, on renwu of the fourth month Venus was visible in daylight,

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年，二月庚寅，太白經天。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Zhou, on gengyin of the second month, Venus crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangshun under Zhou, on gengyin of the second month Venus crossed the meridian at culmination.

sentences.zh: ◎流星

translations.literal: ◎ Shooting Stars
translations.idiomatic: Shooting Stars

sentences.zh: 梁乾化元年，十一月甲辰，東方有流星如數升器，出畢宿口，曳光三丈餘，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianhua of Liang, on jiachen of the eleventh month, in the east there was a shooting star like a vessel of several sheng; it issued from the mouth of the Net mansion, trailing light for more than three zhang, with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianhua under Liang, on jiachen of the eleventh month a meteor like a multi-pint vessel appeared in the east, emerging from the Net asterism's opening, trailing light for more than thirty feet with a thunderous roar.

sentences.zh: 唐長興二年，九月丙戌夜，二鼓初，東北方有小流星入北斗魁滅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing of Tang, on the night of bingxu of the ninth month, at the beginning of the second drum, in the northeast there was a small shooting star that entered the leader of the Northern Dipper and was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changxing under Tang, on the night of bingxu in the ninth month, at the second watch a small meteor entered the Dipper's leader and vanished.

sentences.zh: 至五鼓初，西北方次北有流星，狀如半升器，初小後大，速流如奎滅。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the fifth drum, north-northwest there was a shooting star shaped like a half-sheng vessel, at first small then large, streaming swiftly and being extinguished like the Striding Legs mansion.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth watch, north-northwest, a meteor shaped like a half-pint cup appeared, small at first then swelling as it streaked swiftly and vanished near the Striding Legs asterism.

sentences.zh: 尾跡凝天，屈曲似雲而散，光明燭地。

translations.literal: Its tail-trail congealed in the sky, bending and dispersing like clouds; its brilliance illuminated the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Its wake coiled across the sky, curling like clouds before dispersing, its light bright enough to light the ground.

sentences.zh: 又東北有流星如大桃，出下臺星，西北速流，至斗柄第三星旁滅。

translations.literal: Again in the northeast there was a shooting star like a large peach; it issued from the Lower Terrace star, streamed swiftly northwest, and was extinguished beside the third star of the Dipper's handle.
translations.idiomatic: Another meteor like a large peach rose in the northeast from the Lower Terrace star, streaked northwest, and vanished beside the third star of the Dipper's handle.

sentences.zh: 五鼓後至明，中天及四方有小流星百餘，流註交橫。

translations.literal: From after the fifth drum until dawn, at the center of the sky and in the four directions there were more than a hundred small shooting stars, streaming and crossing one another.
translations.idiomatic: From the fifth watch until dawn, more than a hundred small meteors crossed the zenith and all quarters of the sky in intersecting trails.

sentences.zh: 應順元年春，二月辛未夜，有大星如五升器，流於東北，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Yingshun, on the night of xinwei of the second month, there was a great star like a five-sheng vessel, streaming toward the northeast, with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Yingshun, on the night of xinwei in the second month a great meteor like a five-pint vessel streaked northeast with a thunderous roar.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年，九月辛丑夜，五鼓初，有大星如五斗器而南流，尾跡長數丈，亦赤色，移時盤屈如龍形，蹙縮如二鏵，相鬥而散。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingtai, on the night of xinchou of the ninth month, at the beginning of the fifth drum, there was a great star like a five-dou vessel streaming south; its tail-trail was several zhang in length and also red; after a time it coiled and bent like a dragon's form, contracted like two plowshares fighting, then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingtai, on the night of xinchou in the ninth month, at the fifth watch a great meteor like a bushel measure streamed south, its red tail trailing for many feet; for a while it writhed like a dragon, then contracted like two plow blades clashing before breaking apart.

sentences.zh: 又一星稍小，東流，有尾跡，凝成白氣，食頃方散。

translations.literal: Again a star somewhat smaller streamed east, with a tail-trail that congealed into white vapor and only dispersed after the time of a meal.
translations.idiomatic: A somewhat smaller star followed eastward, its trail condensing into white vapor that took the length of a meal to dissipate.

sentences.zh: 晉天福三年，三月壬申夜，四鼓後，東方有大流星，狀如三升器，其色白，長尺餘，屈曲流出河鼓星東三尺，流丈餘滅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu of Jin, on the night of renshen of the third month, after the fourth drum, in the east there was a great shooting star shaped like a three-sheng vessel; its color was white, its length more than a chi; bending and streaming, it issued three chi east of the Drum at the River star, streamed for more than a zhang, and was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianfu under Jin, on the night of renshen in the third month, after the fourth watch a great white meteor like a three-pint vessel appeared in the east, a little over a foot long; curving outward three feet east of the Drum at the River star, it streaked for more than ten feet and vanished.

sentences.zh: 周顯德元年，正月庚寅，子夜後，東北有大星墜，有聲如雷，牛馬震駭，六街鼓人方寐而驚，以為曉鼓，乃齊伐鼓以應之，至曙方知之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiande of Zhou, on gengyin of the first month, after midnight, in the northeast a great star fell with a sound like thunder; oxen and horses were terrified; the drum-beaters of the Six Streets, just asleep, were startled, thinking it was the dawn drum, and all together beat drums in response; only at daybreak did they learn the truth.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiande under Zhou, on gengyin of the first month, after midnight a great meteor fell in the northeast with a thunderous roar; cattle and horses stampeded; the night-watch drummers of the Six Streets, roused from sleep, mistook it for the dawn signal and beat drums in unison until daybreak revealed the mistake.

sentences.zh: 三月，高平之役，戰之前夕，有大流星如日，流行數丈，墜於賊營之所。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the eve of the battle at Gaoping, there was a great shooting star bright as the sun; it streamed for several zhang and fell upon the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the eve of the Gaoping campaign, a great meteor bright as the sun streaked for many feet and fell in the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: ◎雲氣

translations.literal: ◎ Cloud Vapors
translations.idiomatic: Cloud Vapors and Omens

sentences.zh: 梁開平二年，三月丁丑夜，月有蒼白暈，又有白氣如人形十餘，皆東向，出於暈內。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiping of Liang, on the night of dingchou of the third month, the moon had a pale blue-white halo, and again there were more than ten white vapors shaped like human forms, all facing east, issuing from within the halo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiping under Liang, on the night of dingchou in the third month the moon wore a pale bluish halo, and more than ten white vapors shaped like human figures, all facing east, emerged from within it.

sentences.zh: 九月乙酉，平旦，西方有氣如人形甚眾，皆若俯伏之狀，經刻乃散。

translations.literal: On yiyou of the ninth month, at daybreak, in the west there were very many vapors shaped like human forms, all as if in prostrate posture; after the time of a quarter-hour they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou of the ninth month at dawn, a great host of human-shaped vapors appeared in the west, all seeming to bow prostrate; they dispersed after about fifteen minutes.

sentences.zh: 唐同光三年，日有背氣，凡十二。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang of Tang, the sun had opposing vapors; in all, twelve times.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang under Tang, opposing solar halos appeared twelve times.

sentences.zh: 三年，九月丁未夜，遍天陰雲，北方有聲如雷，四面雞雉皆雊，俗謂之「天狗落」。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the night of dingwei of the ninth month, clouds covered the whole sky; in the north there was a sound like thunder, and on all sides chickens and pheasants crowed; popularly this is called "the celestial dog falling."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on the night of dingwei in the ninth month the sky was wholly overcast; thunder rolled in the north and fowl crowed on every side—the folk called it "the celestial dog falling."

sentences.zh: 是歲，日有背氣，凡十三。

translations.literal: That year, the sun had opposing vapors; in all, thirteen times.
translations.idiomatic: That year opposing solar halos appeared thirteen times.

sentences.zh: 是月，司天監奏：「自七月三日陰雲大雨，至九月十八日後方晴，三辰行度災祥，數日不見。」

translations.literal: That month, the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "From the third day of the seventh month, with overcast clouds and heavy rain, until after the eighteenth day of the ninth month it finally cleared; the motions and degrees of the three luminaries and omens of disaster and blessing could not be seen for several days."
translations.idiomatic: That month the astronomical directorate reported: "From the third day of the seventh month clouds and heavy rain persisted until after the eighteenth of the ninth month; for days we could not observe the sun, moon, and stars or read their omens."

sentences.zh: 閏十二月庚午，日有黑氣，似日，交相錯磨，測在室十度。

translations.literal: On gengwu of the intercalary twelfth month, the sun had black vapor resembling a sun, grinding and crossing one another; measurement placed it at the tenth degree of the Encampment mansion.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu of the intercalary twelfth month a black vapor like a second sun appeared beside the disk, the two grinding against each other; observation placed it at the tenth degree of the Encampment asterism.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，十二月壬辰，西方有赤氣，如火焰焰，約二千里。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng, on renchen of the twelfth month, in the west there was red vapor like blazing flames, extending about two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng, on renchen of the twelfth month red vapor like leaping flames stretched across the western sky for some two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 占者云「不出二年，其下當有大兵。」

translations.literal: The diviners said: "Within two years there will surely be great armies below it."
translations.idiomatic: Diviners said: "Within two years great armies will march in the region beneath it."

sentences.zh: 長興三年，六月，司天監奏：「自月初至月終，每夜陰雲蔽天，不辨星月。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Changxing, in the sixth month, the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "From the beginning of the month to the end of the month, every night overcast clouds covered the sky and stars and moon could not be distinguished."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changxing, in the sixth month the astronomical directorate reported: "From the first to the last night of the month clouds shrouded the sky each night so that neither stars nor moon could be seen."

sentences.zh: 應順元年，四月九日，白虹貫日，是時閔帝遇害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yingshun, on the ninth day of the fourth month, a white rainbow pierced the sun; at that time Emperor Mindi was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yingshun, on the ninth day of the fourth month a white rainbow pierced the sun; at that time Emperor Min was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，高祖將建義於太原，日傍多有五色雲，如蓮芰之狀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu of Jin, when Gaozu was about to raise righteous arms at Taiyuan, beside the sun there were many five-colored clouds shaped like lotus seed-pods.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianfu era, as Jin Gaozu prepared to raise his banner at Taiyuan, five-colored clouds like lotus pods gathered beside the sun.

sentences.zh: 二年，正月丙辰，一鼓初，北方有赤氣，向西至戌亥地，東北至醜地已來向北，闊三丈餘，狀如火光。

translations.literal: In the second year, on bingchen of the first month, at the beginning of the first drum, in the north there was red vapor extending west to the xu and hai regions, and from the northeast to the chou region turning northward, more than three zhang in breadth, shaped like firelight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on bingchen of the first month, at the first watch red vapor appeared in the north, stretching west toward the xu-hai quarter and from the northeast through the chou quarter northward, more than thirty feet wide and like blazing fire.

sentences.zh: 赤氣內見紫微宮共北斗諸星，其氣乍明乍暗。

translations.literal: Within the red vapor could be seen the Purple Forbidden Palace together with the stars of the Northern Dipper; the vapor was now bright, now dim.
translations.idiomatic: Within the red glow the Purple Forbidden Enclosure and the stars of the Northern Dipper could be seen, the vapor brightening and fading by turns.

sentences.zh: 至三點後，後有白氣數條，相次西行，直至三鼓後散。

translations.literal: By after the third point of the night, afterward there were several streaks of white vapor, one after another streaming west, until after the third drum they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: After the third hour several streaks of white vapor followed one another westward until they dispersed after the third watch.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐二年十二月，日暈三重，上有背氣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Qianyou of Han, the sun had a triple halo with opposing vapor above it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Qianyou under Han, the sun showed a triple halo with an opposing arc above it.

sentences.zh: 周顯德三年，十二月庚午，白虹貫日，氣暈勾環。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande of Zhou, on gengwu of the twelfth month, a white rainbow pierced the sun; vaporous halos hooked and ringed around it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande under Zhou, on gengwu of the twelfth month a white rainbow pierced the sun, halos hooking and ringing around the disk.
